# nats

```go
import "github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/stores/nats"
```

Package nats is the NATS JetStream state\-store backend for blkit: a durable, shareable store keeping each run's ProcessState in a JetStream key\-value bucket — a natural fit when NATS is already the message broker. See specs/stores/nats\-state\-store.spec.md.

<a name="New"></a>
### func [New](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/stores/nats/store.go#L44>)

```go
func New(cfg Config) *Store
```

New connects to NATS and creates (or binds to) the bucket, configured with history depth 1 — old revisions of a flipped entry are not needed; the audit story lives in the records themselves. Following the blkit constructor convention it panics on an invalid config or a failed connect.

<a name="Store.CurrentVersion"></a>
### func (\*Store) [CurrentVersion](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/stores/nats/store.go#L297>)

```go
func (s *Store) CurrentVersion(runID string) (*bl.CurrentVersion, error)
```

### func (\*Store) [Flush](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/stores/nats/store.go#L219>)

```go
func (s *Store) Flush(runID string) error
```

<a name="Store.FullHistory"></a>
### func (\*Store) [FullHistory](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/stores/nats/store.go#L323>)

```go
func (s *Store) FullHistory(runID string) (*bl.FullHistory, error)
```

FullHistory reads the run's v. and h. entries and sorts them into replay order (Timestamp, revision). Returns (nil, nil) for an unknown run.

<a name="Store.WriteBatch"></a>
### func (\*Store) [WriteBatch](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/stores/nats/store.go#L120>)

```go
func (s *Store) WriteBatch(ops []bl.WriteOp) error
```

WriteBatch applies the ops one by one — the KV store has no cross\-key batching primitive, which the write contract allows. Each Put waits for the JetStream publish acknowledgement, so an accepted write is already quorum\-accepted and durable — which is why Flush is a no\-op.
